reasoning: compute_local() begins 'if (host_flag) { ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_array(); return; }' (impl header lines 156-162). Its base src/ML-SNAP/compute_grid_local.h declares 'void compute_local() override = 0;' and no compute_array. So the qualified call resolves to Compute's 'virtual void compute_array() {}' (src/compute.h:129) - an empty body. host_flag is set from 'host_flag = (execution_space == HostKK)'; src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos.cpp instantiates ComputeSNAGridLocalKokkosDevice<LMPDeviceType> unconditionally, and on a CPU-only Kokkos build LMPDeviceType==LMPHostType so execution_space==HostKK and the branch is taken. reasoning: Same defect as F0065 (duplicate), and the extra claim about the sibling checks out too. src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:128-132 reads 'void ComputeGaussianGridLocalKokkos<DeviceType>::compute_local() { if (host_flag) { return; } invoked_local = update->ntimestep; ...' - it returns before computing anything, so on a CPU-only Kokkos build gaussian/grid/local/kk likewise leaves alocal unwritten and does not even set invoked_local. reasoning: TagCSNAGridLocalComputeNeigh has two loops 'for (int j = 0; j < ntotal; j++)' (counting pass and fill pass); neither tests atom->mask. The constructor sets 'datamask_read = EMPTY_MASK;' and compute_local() syncs only X_MASK|F_MASK|TYPE_MASK, so mask is never even fetched. The CPU original src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp compute_local() has, as the first statement of the identical j loop, 'if (!(mask[j] & groupbit)) continue;' with 'const int *const mask = atom->mask;' hoisted above. reasoning: Constructor: 'cutsq_tmp = cutsq[1][1]; for (i=1..ntypes) for (j=1..ntypes) { k_cutsq.view_host()(i,j) = k_cutsq.view_host()(j,i) = cutsq_tmp; ... }' - every entry of the (ntypes+1)^2 table gets cutsq[1][1]. The base class really does build a per-type table: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp constructor, 'cut = 2.0*radelem[i]*rcutfac; cutsq[i][i] = cut*cut;' plus the off-diagonal '(radelem[i]+radelem[j])*rcutfac'. And the kernel compounds it: TagCSNAGridLocalComputeNeigh uses 'rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype)' with 'const int itype = 1;' hard-wired a few lines above, i.e. row 1 only, while the CPU cutoff test is 'if (rsq < cutsq[jtype][jtype] && rsq > 1e-20)'. Both halves of the finding hold; with a single atom type the two agree, with differing radelem they do not.
fix: Fill k_cutsq from the real base-class table ('k_cutsq.view_host()(i,j) = cutsq[i][j];' inside the double loop, then modify_host()), and change both kernel tests to 'rnd_cutsq(jtype,jtype)' to match compute_sna_grid_local.cpp. Drop the now-unused cutsq_tmp member.

reasoning: compute_local() has '// max_neighs is defined here - think of more elaborate methods.' followed by 'max_neighs = 100;', and then 'snaKK.grow_rij(chunk_size, max_neighs, padding_factor);' (the line 'snaKK.grow_rij(chunk_size, ntotal);' is commented out directly above it). TagCSNAGridLocalComputeNeigh's second loop runs over all ntotal atoms and writes 'snaKK.rij(ii,offset,0..2)', 'snaKK.wj(ii,offset)', 'snaKK.rcutij(ii,offset)', 'snaKK.inside(ii,offset)' then 'offset++' with no comparison against max_neighs anywhere. The CPU style sizes for the worst case: 'snaptr->grow_rij(ntotal);'. The scratch allocation is also sized 'team_size_compute_neigh * max_neighs'. Two separate consequences: >100 neighbours writes out of bounds, and the downstream ComputeCayleyKlein/ComputeUi range policies are built with extent max_neighs so neighbours 100+ would be silently skipped even if the memory were large enough (d_ninside(ii) is stored unclamped and used as the loop bound in those kernels).
fix: Add a max-reduction over d_ninside (or a cheap pre-pass counting atoms within cutmax of each grid point), take the MPI-local max, and pass that to grow_rij; alternatively pass ntotal as the commented-out line did. As a minimum, clamp offset and raise an error when ninside > max_neighs.

reasoning: All three TagCSNAGridLocalPreUi operator() overloads (3-index, 2-index and 1-index forms) contain 'int itype = type(iatom); int ielem = d_map[itype]; snaKK.pre_ui(iatom, j, ielem);'. iatom is 'iatom_mod + iatom_div*vector_length' bounded by 'if (iatom >= chunk_size) return;' - chunk_size is MIN(chunksize, total_range) grid points, not atoms. The same file states the intended convention in TagCSNAGridLocalComputeNeigh: '// currently, all grid points are type 1 ... const int itype = 1; int ielem = 0; if (chemflag) ielem = d_map[itype];', which matches the CPU code 'const int itype = 1; int ielem = 0; if (chemflag) ielem = map[itype];'. Two failures: (a) the central element is map[type[grid_index]] instead of map[1]; (b) d_map is read even when chemflag is 0, and MemKK::realloc_kokkos uses 'Kokkos::NoInit' (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:429) and d_map is deep-copied only 'if (chemflag)', so with chemflag off ielem is garbage. Also type() has extent nmax, so chunk_size > nmax is an out-of-bounds read. One of these is dispatched for every run - snap_get_policy picks the overload by policy rank at compute_local().
fix: In all three TagCSNAGridLocalPreUi overloads replace the two lines with 'const int ielem = chemflag ? d_map[1] : 0;' (matching the ComputeNeigh convention and the CPU style). Optionally hoist it to a member computed once in compute_local().

reasoning: Constructor: 'MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_radelem,...,nelements); MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_wjelem,...,nelements); MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_sinnerelem,...,nelements); MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_dinnerelem,...,nelements);' then host mirrors are filled by 'for (int i = 1; i <= atom->ntypes; i++) { h_radelem(i-1) = radelem[i]; h_wjelem(i-1) = wjelem[i]; if (switchinnerflag) { h_sinnerelem(i) = sinnerelem[i]; h_dinnerelem(i) = dinnerelem[i]; } }'. nelements is 1 unless the 'chem' keyword is given (src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp sets 'nelements = 1;' in the defaults block and only reassigns it under 'chem'), and it is unrelated to atom->ntypes. Both halves of the claim hold: (a) ntypes > nelements overruns radelem/wjelem, (b) the sinner/dinner writes use index i (1..ntypes) into a length-nelements view, so even ntypes==nelements==1 writes h_sinnerelem(1) one past the end. These are host mirror views allocated with Kokkos::NoInit, so this is a plain heap overflow with no bounds check in a release build.
fix: Size all four views with atom->ntypes (they are indexed by type, not element - see F0077) or with MAX(nelements, atom->ntypes) if the element indexing is kept, and use the same i-1 offset for sinner/dinner as for radelem/wjelem.

MemoryKokkos::create_kokkos(TYPE&, value_type**&, n1, n2, name) (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h) smalloc()s only the row-pointer array and sets 'array[i] = &h_data(i,0)', i.e. row 0 points into the Kokkos View's host allocation. Memory::destroy(TYPE**&) does 'sfree(array[0]); sfree(array);'. So on the second setup() (Modify::setup() calls compute[i]->setup() on every run) deallocate() free()s a pointer that was never malloc()ed. The leak of the base-class array on the first setup() is real too. The sibling confirms the intent: compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h setup() opens with '// Do not call ComputeGrid::setup(), we don't wanna allocate the grid array there.' and calls only set_grid_global()/set_grid_local(). Grid coordinate columns are already written by TagCSNAGridLocalComputeNeigh, so the dropped assign_coords() is not needed on the device path. Apply the identical change in compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp.

reasoning: TagCSNAGridLocalComputeNeigh fill loop: 'int jelem = 0; if (chemflag) jelem = d_map[jtype]; ... snaKK.wj(ii,offset) = d_wjelem[jelem]; snaKK.rcutij(ii,offset) = (2.0*d_radelem[jelem])*rcutfac;' with a comment admitting the choice ('pair snap uses jelem here, but we use jtype, see compute_sna_grid.cpp / actually since the views here have values starting at 0, let's use jelem'). The CPU original is unambiguous: 'snaptr->wj[ninside] = wjelem[jtype]; snaptr->rcutij[ninside] = 2.0 * radelem[jtype] * rcutfac;'. So whenever two types map to the same element they get identical weights/radii on the device but distinct ones on the CPU. The off-by-one interaction is real as well: the mirrors were filled with h_wjelem(i-1)=wjelem[i], so with chemflag off (jelem always 0) every neighbour gets wjelem[1]/radelem[1] regardless of type. Note the neighbouring sinnerij/dinnerij lines diverge from the CPU too (KOKKOS averages ielem and jelem, the CPU uses sinnerelem[jelem] alone), which is a further instance of the same class of defect.
fix: Index by type: 'snaKK.wj(ii,offset) = d_wjelem[jtype-1]; snaKK.rcutij(ii,offset) = 2.0*d_radelem[jtype-1]*rcutfac;' after sizing d_wjelem/d_radelem with atom->ntypes (see F0070), or drop the -1 offset and size them ntypes+1 so the indexing reads like the CPU code. Also reconcile sinnerij/dinnerij with compute_sna_grid_local.cpp.

reasoning: KOKKOS kernel: 'const KK_FLOAT imass = rmass[i];' ... 'const KK_FLOAT jmass = rmass[j];' ... 'KK_FLOAT meff = imass*jmass / (imass+jmass); if (mask_i & freeze_group_bit) meff = jmass; if (mask[j] & freeze_group_bit) meff = imass;'. The CPU base src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hooke.cpp has, under the comment '// meff = effective mass of pair of particles / if I or J part of rigid body, use body mass': 'mi = rmass[i]; mj = rmass[j]; if (fix_rigid) { if (mass_rigid[i] > 0.0) mi = mass_rigid[i]; if (mass_rigid[j] > 0.0) mj = mass_rigid[j]; } meff = mi*mj/(mi+mj);', and the top of PairGranHooke::compute() refreshes mass_rigid from fix_rigid->extract("body")/extract("masstotal") on every reneighbor followed by comm->forward_comm(this). 'grep -n "mass_rigid\|fix_rigid" src/KOKKOS/pair_gran*' returns nothing, so no compensating path exists. PairGranHookeKokkos::init_style() calls PairGranHooke::init_style() (which reaches PairGranHookeHistory::init_style where fix_rigid is looked up and assigned) and then only adjusts the neighbor request and rejects FULL lists - there is no guard rejecting fix_rigid. meff feeds both the normal damping 'damp = meff*gamman_kk*vnnr*rsqinv' and the friction cap 'fs = meff*gammat_kk*vrel', so the divergence changes forces.
fix: Port the rigid-body mass path: add a DAT::tdual_float_1d k_mass_rigid filled in compute() when (fix_rigid && neighbor->ago == 0) from fix_rigid->extract("body")/("masstotal") plus the existing forward_comm, sync it to the device, and in the kernel use 'KK_FLOAT mi = imass, mj = jmass; if (fix_rigid_flag) { if (d_mass_rigid[i] > 0.0) mi = d_mass_rigid[i]; if (d_mass_rigid[j] > 0.0) mj = d_mass_rigid[j]; }' before forming meff. Apply to all three KOKKOS granular styles (see F0499). As an interim measure, add 'if (fix_rigid) error->all(FLERR,"Pair style gran/hooke/kk does not (yet) support fix rigid");' at the end of init_style().

reasoning: src/pair.h:247 declares 'int special_lj[4];    // copied from force->special_lj for Kokkos'. Neither pair_gran_hooke_kokkos.h nor pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.h nor pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos.h declares a shadowing member (grep for special_lj in those three headers returns nothing), while pair_lj_cut_kokkos.h:91 and pair_gauss_cut_kokkos.h:89 both declare 'KK_FLOAT special_lj[4];'. So the four assignments in compute() ('special_lj[0] = force->special_lj[0]; ...') convert force->special_lj's doubles to int. The kernel then reads 'KK_FLOAT factor_lj = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(special_lj[sbmask(j)]); ... if (factor_lj == 0) continue;' and, further down, actually scales with it ('fx *= factor_lj; ... tor3 *= factor_lj;'), exactly like the CPU style which uses 'double *special_lj = force->special_lj;'. So a factor of 0.5 becomes 0 and the pair is skipped entirely; 1.5 would become 1. Reachability requires bonded granular particles (e.g. atom_style hybrid sphere bond) with a fractional special_bonds lj factor, which is why I keep this at medium rather than high, but the truncation itself is unambiguous. All three KOKKOS granular styles are affected identically (lines 125-128 / 142-145 / 142-145).
fix: Add 'KK_FLOAT special_lj[4];' as a protected member of PairGranHookeKokkos, PairGranHookeHistoryKokkos and PairGranHertzHistoryKokkos (shadowing Pair::special_lj the way pair_lj_cut_kokkos.h does), so the four copies in compute() keep full precision.

reasoning: The premise 'the flat alias of x is layout-dependent' is false: atom->x is pinned to LayoutRight independently of KOKKOS_LAYOUT. src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.h:34 declares 'DAT::ttransform_kkfloat_1d_3_lr k_x;', and src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:1257 defines 'typedef TransformView<KK_FLOAT*[3], double*[3], Kokkos::LayoutRight> ttransform_kkfloat_1d_3_lr;' - the layout parameter is the literal Kokkos::LayoutRight, not LMPDeviceLayout. TransformView (kokkos_type.h:698) uses that parameter directly: 'typedef Kokkos::DualView<KKType, KKLayout, KKSpace> kk_view;', so k_x.view_device() is a LayoutRight view under every build and 'xvec = DAT::t_kkfloat_1d(d_x.data(),nvec)' is always the correct [x0,y0,z0,x1,...] flattening. Force is the odd one out: atom_kokkos.h:36 'DAT::ttransform_kkacc_1d_3 k_f;' and kokkos_type.h:1258 'typedef TransformView<KK_ACC_FLOAT*[3], double*[3], LMPDeviceLayout> ttransform_kkacc_1d_3;' - layout-dependent, hence the flat fvec alias needs a guard. That is exactly what the existing branches do, and the flag is even named for it: min_kokkos.h:27 'F_LAYOUTRIGHT'. I checked every one of the 11 'if constexpr (F_LAYOUTRIGHT)' sites (min_kokkos.cpp:624/661/698, min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:191/286/442, min_cg_kokkos.cpp:68/125/178, min_sd_kokkos.cpp:51) and the guarded branch is 'auto l_fvec = fvec;' in all 11 - not one guards xvec. The asymmetry the finding reads as a missing guard is the intended design. Note also that the 'ghost x-coordinates corrupted' scenario could not arise anyway: even under LayoutLeft, x has nmax rows, so a flat length-3*nlocal window stays inside the allocation.

Duplicate of F0094 and refuted for the same reason. The x DualView is declared with an explicit Kokkos::LayoutRight (atom_kokkos.h:34 'DAT::ttransform_kkfloat_1d_3_lr k_x;' -> kokkos_type.h:1257 'TransformView<KK_FLOAT*[3], double*[3], Kokkos::LayoutRight>'), so KOKKOS_LAYOUT=default does not change it and the flat xvec alias built in reset_vectors() is valid on CUDA/HIP as well. Only k_f carries LMPDeviceLayout, which is why the F_LAYOUTRIGHT guards exist and why all of them wrap fvec loops rather than xvec loops. The cited 'guarded loops at 191, 286, 442' are all fvec reductions; the 'unguarded loops at 253/392/411' are all xvec loops. No fix is needed.

Read both sides in full. CPU PairCoulDSF::compute(): 'prefactor = qqrd2e * qtmp * q[j] / r; ... forcecoul = prefactor * (erfcc/r + 2.0*alpha/MY_PIS*erfcd + r*f_shift) * r; if (factor_coul < 1.0) forcecoul -= (1.0 - factor_coul) * prefactor;' and 'ecoul = prefactor * (erfcc - r*e_shift - rsq*f_shift); if (factor_coul < 1.0) ecoul -= (1.0 - factor_coul) * prefactor;'. PairCoulDSF::single() uses the identical convention, so it is not a compute/single inconsistency in the CPU style. KOKKOS: 'const KK_FLOAT prefactor = factor_coul * qqrd2e*qtmp*q[j]/r;' and then forcecoul/ecoul are formed from that prefactor with no subtraction anywhere in the kernel (I read the whole loop body, lines 244-292; the only other use of factor_coul is the sbmask fetch). Writing P for qqrd2e*qi*qj/r and X for the damped/shifted bracket, CPU gives P*X-(1-fc)*P while KOKKOS gives fc*P*X. These agree only at fc==1; at the LAMMPS default special coul 0.0 the CPU contributes -P and KOKKOS contributes 0. The intended KOKKOS pattern exists in the sibling: pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp has 'const KK_FLOAT prefactor = qqrd2e*qtmp*q(j)/r;' (unscaled) followed by 'forcecoul -= (1.0-factor_coul)*prefactor;' and 'ecoul -= (1.0-factor_coul)*prefactor;'. The second half of the finding checks out too: pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:223 and :248 both do 'const KK_FLOAT prefactor = factor_coul * qqrd2e * qtmp * q(j);' with no subtraction, against pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf.cpp:137-143/164-165 which does it correctly.
fix: In pair_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp change line 260 to 'const KK_FLOAT prefactor = qqrd2e*qtmp*q[j]/r;', make forcecoul and ecoul non-const, and after each add 'if (factor_coul < 1.0) forcecoul -= (static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(1.0)-factor_coul)*prefactor;' / '... ecoul -= ...', copying pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:213 and :262. Make the same change in pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp compute_fcoul()/compute_ecoul() (lines 223 and 248); note those two helpers return a value divided by r, so the subtraction must be folded in before the division.

reasoning: Duplicate of F0317; verified independently against src/pair_coul_dsf.cpp compute() and single() and against src/KOKKOS/pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp (the correctly ported sibling). reasoning: The code is as quoted: get_kinetic_energy()'s per-type branch is 'atomKK->sync(execution_space, TYPE_MASK); ... mass = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>();' with the author's own comment '// D.I. : why is there no MASS_MASK ?' immediately above, and no k_mass.sync anywhere in the file (the file's only sync calls are lines 60, 70, 88, 143). I confirmed there is no MASS_MASK bit: src/atom_masks.h has RMASS_MASK (0x200) but no MASS_MASK, so AtomKokkos::sync() cannot cover k_mass and it must be synced by hand. The convention is clear across the package - about twenty styles do 'atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()' explicitly (compute_temp_kokkos.cpp:46, compute_ke_kokkos.cpp:65, fix_baoab_kokkos.cpp:92, group_kokkos.h:64, ...) and AtomKokkos::set_mass() marks k_mass.modify_host() (atom_kokkos.cpp:287-316). Note the sibling branch in the same function does it right for rmass via RMASS_MASK, which makes the omission an oversight rather than a deliberate choice. I did try to refute this on reachability and it is narrow in practice: FixNVEKokkos::init() (fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46) and FixNHKokkos (fix_nh_kokkos.cpp:77-78) both do 'k_mass.modify_host(); k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();' at every init, so in a normal KOKKOS run the device copy is already fresh when end_of_step runs. The failure needs a configuration where no other device consumer has synced the masses. Hence I downgrade the severity, but the missing sync is real and the fix is one line.
fix: In get_kinetic_energy(), add 'atomKK->k_mass.template sync<DeviceType>();' immediately after 'atomKK->sync(execution_space, TYPE_MASK);' (line 70), and replace the '// D.I. : why is there no MASS_MASK ?' comment. Match src/KOKKOS/group_kokkos.h:63-64.

reasoning: The missing 'atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()' is real - it is the same one as F0198 - but the description of what it affects and the failure scenario are both wrong. (a) Location: lines 70-77 are inside the file-static get_kinetic_energy(), which computes the kinetic energy for the 'rescale' option, not the group mass. (b) The group mass is computed at end_of_step():97 by 'masstotal = groupKK->mass_kk<DeviceType>(igroup);', and GroupKokkos::mass_kk (src/KOKKOS/group_kokkos.h:59-68) does sync correctly: 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,MASK_MASK|TYPE_MASK); atomKK->k_mass.template sync<DeviceType>();' before the reduction. So the group-mass path is not defective. (c) The claimed NaN cannot occur even hypothetically: end_of_step():101 is 'if (masstotal == 0.0) return;', so a zero group mass causes an early return, not a division by zero. The real consequence of the actual defect is a wrong ekin_old/ekin_new and hence a wrong rescale factor, only when 'rescale' is on. As with F0198, reachability is limited because FixNVEKokkos::init() and FixNHKokkos both force a k_mass device copy at every init.
fix: Same single line as F0198: add 'atomKK->k_mass.template sync<DeviceType>();' after the TYPE_MASK sync at line 70 in get_kinetic_energy(). No change is needed for the group-mass path.

reasoning: Verified every link in the chain. Declarations: src/KOKKOS/meam_kokkos.h:65 'typename AT::t_int_2d d_scale;' and src/KOKKOS/pair_meam_kokkos.h:108 'typename AT::t_int_2d d_scale;' - an integer view. Source: PairMEAM::scale is 'double **' (src/MEAM/pair_meam.cpp:170 'memory->create(scale, np1, np1, "pair:scale");'). Fill: PairMEAMKokkos<DeviceType>::coeff() does 'auto h_scale = Kokkos::create_mirror_view(d_scale); ... h_scale(i,j) = scale[i][j];' - an implicit double->int narrowing. Use: it is consumed as a floating-point multiplier, meam_dens_final_kokkos.h:59-63 'KK_FLOAT scaleii; ... scaleii = d_scale(type[i],type[i]);' then :182 'Fl *= scaleii;', and meam_force_kokkos.h:187-188 'KK_FLOAT scaleij = d_scale(type[i], type[i]); KK_FLOAT phi_sc = phi * scaleij;'. So 0.5 truncates to 0 and 1.9 to 1. The fix-adapt exposure is real: src/MEAM/pair_meam.cpp:898 'if (strcmp(str, "scale") == 0) return (void *) scale;' and doc/src/fix_adapt.rst:243 lists meam/scale as a type-pair adapt target. Nothing compensates: I checked all uses of d_scale and there is no rounding, no separate double path, and no error/warning for meam/kk + fix adapt. There is a second, arguably worse half that the finding notes only in passing and that I confirmed: d_scale is deep-copied ONLY inside coeff() (pair_meam_kokkos.cpp:299-310); nothing re-copies it later, so a fix adapt scale change never reaches the device at all, even for integral values. The default is benign because PairMEAM::coeff sets scale[i][j] = 1.0 (pair_meam.cpp:310) before the copy.
fix: Change d_scale to a floating-point view - 'typename AT::t_kkfloat_2d d_scale;' in src/KOKKOS/meam_kokkos.h:65 and src/KOKKOS/pair_meam_kokkos.h:108, and the matching parameter type in the meam_dens_final signature (meam_dens_final_kokkos.h:25 and the declaration in meam_kokkos.h). Then move the scale->d_scale deep_copy out of coeff() into a small helper called from PairMEAMKokkos::compute() (or init_one/init_style plus a per-step refresh) so fix adapt changes actually reach the device.

reasoning: Read both sides. The functor is 'template <class DeviceType, class T> struct FixWallRegionKokkosFunctor { ... FixWallRegionKokkos<DeviceType> c; T *regionKK; FixWallRegionKokkosFunctor(FixWallRegionKokkos<DeviceType>* c_ptr, T *regionKK): value_count(10), c(*c_ptr), regionKK(regionKK) {} ... KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION void operator()(const int i, value_type result) const { c.wall_particle(regionKK,i,result); } };'. Note the asymmetry the finding points at: the fix is copied by value ('c(*c_ptr)') while the region is kept as a raw pointer. That pointer comes from fix_wall_region_kokkos.cpp post_force(): 'if (auto *regionKK = dynamic_cast<RegBlockKokkos<DeviceType>*>(region)) { FixWallRegionKokkosFunctor<...> functor(this,regionKK); Kokkos::parallel_reduce(nlocal,functor,result); }' - region is an ordinary host-heap object from Domain's region factory. Inside the kernel, FixWallRegionKokkos<DeviceType>::wall_particle() calls 'regionKK->match_kokkos(...)' and 'regionKK->surface_kokkos(...)', and those methods (src/KOKKOS/region_block_kokkos.h:67-73, 76-117) read instance members - boxremap (a RegionRemapKokkos by value), dynamic, openflag, interior, rotateflag, and the block bounds via k_inside/surface_interior_kokkos. That is a host-address dereference from device code. FixWallRegionKokkos<LMPDeviceType> is instantiated unconditionally at the bottom of the .cpp, so this is the GPU path, not a host-only one. The established pattern is exactly what the finding says: RegBlockKokkos<DeviceType>::match_all_kokkos (src/KOKKOS/region_block_kokkos.cpp:35-50) sets 'copymode = 1; Kokkos::parallel_for(Kokkos::RangePolicy<DeviceType, TagRegBlockMatchAll>(0,nlocal),*this);' - the region copies ITSELF into the kernel - and the region-aware fixes go through it (fix_setforce_kokkos.cpp:84-92 'regionKKBase->match_all_kokkos(groupbit,k_match);'). I could not find any compensating mechanism (no UVM assumption in the file, no host-only guard, no managed allocation for regions).
fix: Store the region by value in the functor: change 'T *regionKK;' to 'T regionKK;' with 'regionKK(*region_ptr)' in the ctor, set region_ptr->copymode = 1 around the parallel_reduce so the functor copy's destructor does not free the region's arrays, and change FixWallRegionKokkos::wall_particle's template parameter use from 'regionKK->' to 'regionKK.' (the MAXCONTACT lookup becomes 'T::MAXCONTACT' instead of 'std::remove_pointer_t<T>::MAXCONTACT'). Alternatively restructure so the loop is launched from inside the region class as match_all_kokkos does.
